# 6–8 Week Move Calendar: Synchable Reminders

I'm setting **Week 1 = today (May 7, 2026)** and **Move Day = Saturday, July 18, 2026** (10 weeks out). Adjust if your date shifts. I've grouped by week with specific suggested days and times so you can drop them straight into Google Calendar or Apple Reminders.

turns.text:
# Room-by-Room Packing Checklist with Declutter Tips

**How this works:** Each room gets a declutter pass first, then a packing pass. I've split packing into two waves — **Early Pack** (non-essentials, 4–6 weeks out) and **Final Pack** (last week). Every box should be labeled with: **Room name + contents summary + box number + FRAGILE if applicable.** Keep a running numbered inventory on your phone or a clipboard.

---

## 🍳 KITCHEN

**Responsible:** J (joint) — this is the biggest room and goes faster with two people
**Estimated time:** 4–6 hours total (split across 2–3 sessions)
**Priority:** HIGH — start early because it has the most items and the most declutter potential

---

### Declutter Pass (do this first, 1–1.5 hrs)

- [ ] Pull everything out of each cabinet one shelf at a time
- [ ] **Toss:** chipped or cracked dishes, melted spatulas, rusty utensils, stained tupperware without lids, expired spices and food, duplicate can openers, mystery takeout sauce packets, anything sticky or broken
- [ ] **Donate:** duplicate sets of dishes, appliances you haven't used in 12 months (bread maker, fondue pot, juicer), cookbooks you've never opened, excess mugs and water bottles, mismatched silverware
- [ ] **Sell:** high-value small appliances in good condition (KitchenAid, Instant Pot, cast iron you won't ship)
- [ ] **Give to neighbors:** open pantry items, spices, cleaning supplies, half-used rolls of foil and wrap

**Declutter gut-check:** If you have more than one of something and you haven't used the second one in a year, the second one goes. Moving a $12 blender 2,400 miles costs more in space and weight than replacing it.

---

### Early Pack — 4 to 6 weeks out (1.5–2 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| K-1 | Baking supplies: cake pans, muffin tins, cookie sheets, rolling pin, mixing bowls | Nest bowls. Put parchment paper between pans to prevent scratching. |
| K-2 | Specialty appliances: stand mixer, blender, food processor | Original boxes are ideal. Otherwise wrap in towels and pack snugly so nothing shifts. Remove blades, wrap separately in cardboard and tape, and label "SHARP." |
| K-3 | Entertaining items: serving platters, punch bowl, wine glasses, candle holders | Wrap each glass individually in packing paper. Place upright in cells or stuff paper between them. Mark FRAGILE on all sides and top. |
| K-4 | Cookbooks, recipe binders, decorative items | Small box. Books are heavy — never fill a large box with only books. |
| K-5 | Seasonal or rarely used items: holiday cookie cutters, canning supplies, specialty gadgets | One small or medium box. If you hesitate, ask yourself when you last used it. |

---

### Final Pack — last 3 to 5 days (1.5–2 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| K-6 | Everyday dishes: plates, bowls, mugs (the set you kept out) | Stack plates vertically like records — they break less. Wrap each piece. Pad the bottom and top of the box with crumpled paper or towels. Mark FRAGILE. |
| K-7 | Pots, pans, lids, daily utensils, cutting board | Nest pots. Put a layer of paper between each. Wrap lids together. Rubber-band utensils. |
| K-8 | Knives, sharp tools, peeler, grater | Wrap each blade in cardboard and tape it shut. Label "SHARP" on the outside. Or use blade guards. |
| K-9 | Small countertop appliances: toaster, coffee maker, kettle | Empty water from coffee maker. Wrap cords and tape them to the appliance so they don't swing. |
| K-10 | Under-sink items: dish soap, sponges, trash bags, cleaning supplies | Zip-lock any liquids. Pack upright. Label "CLEANING — OPEN EARLY." |
| K-11 | Junk drawer and miscellaneous | Zip-lock small items (batteries, twist ties, rubber bands, takeout menus). Toss what you don't need. |
| K-LAST | Pantry food (non-perishable, sealed) | Use a sturdy small box — cans are heavy. If the item costs less than $3 to replace, consider leaving it. |

**Labeling rule for kitchen:** Mark every kitchen box with a **K** prefix and number. Write "FRAGILE" on any box with glass or ceramic. Write "OPEN FIRST" on the box with coffee maker, mugs, paper towels, and snacks — you'll want that box within 10 minutes of arriving.

---

## 🛋️ LIVING ROOM

**Responsible:** J (joint) — partner focuses on electronics and cables, you focus on decor and shelving
**Estimated time:** 3–4 hours total (split across 2 sessions)
**Priority:** MEDIUM-HIGH — lots of fragile items and electronics that need careful wrapping

---

### Declutter Pass (do this first, 45 min–1 hr)

- [ ] Pull everything off shelves and surfaces
- [ ] **Toss:** dead batteries, old magazines and catalogs, dried-out markers, broken picture frames, candles burned to the nub, tangled cords to unknown devices, dead remotes, instruction manuals (they're all online now)
- [ ] **Donate:** DVDs and Blu-rays you've ripped or never rewatch, board games missing pieces, books you won't reread, throw pillows and blankets you don't love, decor that doesn't fit your taste anymore
- [ ] **Sell:** electronics in good condition (speakers, gaming consoles, monitors), furniture you're not moving
- [ ] **Recycle:** old electronics at a certified e-waste drop-off, not in the trash

**Declutter gut-check:** Hold each decorative item and ask: "Would I buy this again today?" If no, it doesn't earn a spot on the truck.

---

### Early Pack — 4 to 6 weeks out (1–1.5 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| LR-1 | Books and coffee table books | Small boxes only. Fill gaps with packing paper so books don't shift. Spine down for paperbacks. |
| LR-2 | Framed photos and wall art (non-high-value) | Wrap each frame in bubble wrap. Place cardboard corners on frame edges. Stand upright in box like a record — never lay flat and stack. Mark FRAGILE and "THIS SIDE UP." |
| LR-3 | Decorative items: vases, sculptures, candles, bookends | Wrap individually. Fill all empty space so nothing moves when you shake the box. If it rattles, add more paper. |
| LR-4 | Board games, puzzles, cards | Rubber-band game boxes shut. Bag loose pieces. Medium box. |
| LR-5 | Shelving hardware, brackets, curtain rods, hooks | Zip-lock all screws and bolts. Tape the bag to the item it belongs to. Take a photo of your curtain rod bracket setup before removing — you'll forget the spacing. |
| LR-6 | Throw blankets, decorative pillows, couch covers (extras) | Use these as padding in other boxes or stuff them into garbage bags to save box space. They're great cushioning for fragile items. |

---

### Final Pack — last 3 to 5 days (1–1.5 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| LR-7 (P responsible) | TV, soundbar, streaming devices, remotes | Original TV box is ideal. If you don't have it, buy a TV box or wrap in moving blankets. Never lay a flat-screen face-down. Transport upright. Take a photo of the back of the TV and all cable connections before unplugging. Zip-lock all remotes together with batteries removed. |
| LR-8 (P responsible) | Gaming console, controllers, cables | Wrap the console in a towel. Coil each cable separately and secure with a twist-tie or velcro strap. Label which cable goes to what. |

## General Packing Principles (Apply to Every Room)

**Box rules:**
- Heavy items in small boxes, light items in large boxes — no exceptions
- Fill every box completely so it doesn't crush when stacked, but don't over-pack so it bursts
- Tape the bottom of every box with an H-pattern (one strip lengthwise, two strips across) — the single-strip bottom is the number one cause of box blowouts
- Never pack liquids, flammables, or perishables in the moving truck

**Labeling system:**
- Room abbreviation + box number + 2–3 word contents + FRAGILE if applicable
- Example: **K-6 / Everyday Dishes / FRAGILE**
- Write on two sides and the top of every box
- Use a different color marker or tape for each room if you want visual sorting

**Inventory:**
- Keep a simple numbered list on your phone (Google Sheets or Notes app)
- Format: Box number → contents summary → value estimate for insurance
- Photograph the inside of each box before taping it shut — this takes 5 seconds and can save an insurance claim

**Weight test:** If you can't comfortably lift the box to waist height, it's too heavy. Repack.

# Garage / Outdoor / Shed (Continued)

---

**Declutter gut-check (continued):** Garages are the graveyard of "I'll fix this someday" projects. If the item has been sitting broken for 6+ months, you're not going to fix it in Oregon either. Let it go. Also remember: **movers will not transport hazardous materials.** That includes gasoline, propane, paint thinner, pesticides, fertilizer, pool chemicals, ammunition, and fireworks. You must dispose of these before the move or give them away.

---

### Early Pack — 4 to 6 weeks out (1–1.5 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| GA-1 | Hand tools: hammer, screwdrivers, pliers, wrenches, tape measure, level | Wrap sharp tools in towels or cardboard sheaths. Heavy — use a small box. Put your most-used basic toolkit aside for the car kit (you'll need a screwdriver, pliers, box cutter, and hammer on arrival). |
| GA-2 | Power tools: drill, sander, circular saw, jigsaw | Remove batteries and pack them separately — lithium batteries can be a fire risk in hot trucks. Wrap cords around tools and secure with velcro or zip-ties. Original cases are ideal. |
| GA-3 | Lawn and garden: trowels, pruners, garden gloves, pots, seeds | Clean soil off everything — Oregon has agricultural inspection concerns at some points. Dump potting soil and don't transport open bags of soil or mulch. |
| GA-4 | Sports and recreation: bikes, camping gear, fishing rods, ski equipment | Deflate bike tires slightly for altitude changes on the drive. Remove pedals and turn handlebars sideways to save truck space. Bag all small parts. Fishing rods go in hard cases or PVC tubes taped shut. |
| GA-5 | Seasonal items: holiday inflatables, extension cords, outdoor lights | Test lights before packing — no point in moving dead strands. Wrap each strand around a piece of cardboard to prevent tangling. |
| GA-6 | Automotive: jumper cables, jack, tire iron, washer fluid, car cleaning supplies | Keep jumper cables and a flashlight in the car, not the truck. Don't pack fluids in the moving truck — use them up, give them away, or dispose safely. |

---

### Final Pack — last week (1 hr)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| GA-7 | Workbench items: vise, clamps, sandpaper, hardware organizer | Hardware organizers with small drawers — tape every drawer shut individually with painter's tape. If even one pops open, you'll spend an hour on your knees picking up screws. |
| GA-8 | Shelving, pegboard hooks, wall-mounted storage hardware | Zip-lock all mounting hardware. Photograph your pegboard layout if you want to replicate it. |
| GA-9 | Last items: broom, dustpan, step stool, vacuum, mop | Keep the broom and dustpan out until the final sweep. Literally the last things to load. Empty and clean the vacuum — you don't want Ohio dust mites starting a new life in Oregon. |

### Large Garage Items — No Box Needed

| Item | Tip |
|---|---|
| Bicycles | Remove pedals, turn handlebars, deflate tires slightly. Wrap chains in a rag so they don't grease other items. Load upright in the truck and strap down. |
| Workbench | Empty completely. If it disassembles, take it apart and bag hardware. If it doesn't, wrap legs and edges. |
| Shelving units | Disassemble. Bundle shelves with cardboard between them. Bag and label hardware for each unit separately. |
| Grill | Clean thoroughly. Remove propane tank and do not transport it — give it away or exchange it in Oregon. Tape lid shut. Wrap in a moving blanket. |
| Lawn mower | Drain all fuel and oil completely. Disconnect spark plug. Movers and truck rental companies will refuse to load it with fuel. If it's a cheap push mower, consider selling it and buying new in Oregon — the shipping cost may exceed its value. |
| Ladders | Load along the truck wall and strap down. Good for creating a wall-brace for other items. |
| Trash cans and recycling bins | Clean them. Use them as packing containers for unbreakable items like garden tools, brooms, and sports equipment. Free box space. |

**🐕 Pet note:** Garages often store dog crates, travel kennels, outdoor tie-outs, spare leashes, and large bags of food. Decide now whether the crate is coming (yes if you use it regularly or for travel). Pack the crate last — it may ride in the car for the dog. If you have a large bag of food that's mostly full, pour portions into zip-lock bags for the road trip and pack the rest sealed in a box labeled "DOG — OPEN FIRST." Dispose of old or recalled food.

**Responsible:** P (partner)
**Estimated time:** 1–1.5 hours total (mostly final-week work)

- [ ] **Donate:** cleaning supplies you won't finish, working small appliances you don't want (steamer, spare iron)
- [ ] **Leave for the next tenant:** partially full bottles of detergent, dryer sheets, stain remover, fabric softener — not worth the weight

**Declutter gut-check:** This room accumulates supplies faster than any other. If you have 4 partial bottles of detergent, consolidate into one and leave the rest. Moving liquids is heavy, leak-prone, and not worth it.

---

### Early Pack — 4 to 6 weeks out (15–20 min)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| LU-1 | Spare cleaning supplies, broom attachments, mop heads, rags | Only pack sealed items in the truck. Use rags as packing padding elsewhere. |
| LU-2 | Iron, steamer, drying rack, lint rollers, sewing kit | Wrap the iron's soleplate in a towel. Empty any water reservoir. Coil cords. |

---

### Final Pack — last 2 to 3 days (30–45 min)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| LU-3 | Laundry baskets, hampers | Use these as packing containers — fill with soft items like towels, rags, stuffed animals, or dog bedding. Free box space. |
| LU-4 | Remaining detergent, dryer balls, stain pen | Zip-lock all liquids. Only bring what's sealed and worth the space. |
| LU-LAST | Cleaning supplies you used for move-out cleaning | These are literally the last things you pack. Keep a spray bottle, paper towels, trash bags, broom, and dustpan out until you walk out the door. Consider leaving them for the next tenant. |

### Appliance Notes (Washer and Dryer)

| Item | Tip |
|---|---|
| Washer | **48 hours before move:** Run an empty cycle. Disconnect and drain hoses completely. Leave the door open to air-dry the drum. **On move day:** Install transit bolts if you have them (they prevent the drum from moving in transit — check your manual or look up your model). Tape the power cord to the back. Tape the door shut. Move upright only. |
| Dryer | Disconnect and clean the lint trap and exhaust hose. Tape the door shut. Tape the cord to the back. If gas, have the gas line professionally disconnected. |
| Hot water heater | You're almost certainly not moving this — it stays with the house. Confirm with your landlord. |
| Furnace filters | Leave a clean one for the next tenant. Buy one for the Oregon place and have it ready. |

**🐕 Pet note:** If you wash the dog's bedding and blankets regularly, do one final wash 2 days before the move so the dog has a clean, familiar-smelling blanket for the car ride. Don't wash it with heavy scent detergent — the familiar smell is the point.

# 📋 DECLUTTER CHECKLIST TEMPLATE (Google Docs)

*Copy and paste this paragraph into a Google Doc. Duplicate it for each room.*

---

**Room: [ROOM NAME] — Declutter Checklist**
Pull everything out of every drawer, shelf, cabinet, and storage area in this room. Sort into four piles: **KEEP** (pack it), **DONATE** (working, clean, useful — schedule a drop-off or pickup), **SELL** (worth $20+ and you have time to list it on Marketplace, Craigslist, or Nextdoor), and **TRASH/RECYCLE** (broken, expired, stained, incomplete, or not worth anyone's time). For every item in the KEEP pile, ask: *"Have I used this in the last 12 months? Would I buy it again today? Is it worth the cost per pound to ship 2,400 miles?"* If the answer to all three is no, move it to DONATE or TRASH. Take a photo of the room before and after the declutter pass. Note anything you need to buy for the new place. Bag and label DONATE items immediately so they don't creep back into the KEEP pile. Schedule a donation pickup or drop-off date and put it on the calendar. Done is better than perfect — if you're agonizing over an item for more than 30 seconds, it goes.
